is_anopheles.evidence: The review covers Culicidae including Anopheles species (such as An. arabiensis, An. gambiae s.s., An. funestus, etc.) in Mauritania (page 1, 3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Mentions kdr point mutations L1014S and L1014F and ace-1 in the literature review section on insecticide susceptibility (page 8, citing reference 47).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No extractable genotype frequencies or counts (RR, RS, SS) are presented; the paper only summarizes findings previously reported in the literature (e.g. Mint Lekweiry et al. 2016 [47]) without numeric counts or frequencies.

african_field_population.evidence: The literature discussed focuses on mosquito populations collected in Mauritania (pages 1-8).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a review article: 'Mosquitoes (Diptera: Culicidae) in Mauritania: a review of their biodiversity, distribution and medical importance' (page 1, labelled 'REVIEW'). It reviews literature from 1948 to 2016 rather than reporting primary empirical data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Sites and regions such as Nouakchott, Hodh Elgharbi, Tagant, etc. are cited throughout (pages 3-8).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The review synthesizes data collected across decades (1948-2016) without presenting an extractable primary dataset tied to a <=3-year collection window.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Not applicable as this is a review paper.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary data needed; paper is a narrative literature review.

assessment.summary: This article is a comprehensive review of mosquito biodiversity, distribution, and vector status in Mauritania from 1948 to 2016. Because it is a review and does not present primary extractable genotype data, it is not eligible.
exclusion_reasons: Paper is a review article rather than a primary empirical study.
No extractable genotype counts or frequencies with sample sizes are reported.
